text: Situated within the highly regarded sought-after coastal village of Mullion, this spacious, well presented three bedroom home is being offered for sale chain-free. Offering generous and versatile accommodation, this property is ideally suited for family living or those seeking a property in a desirable part of Cornwall. The property also presents an excellent opportunity for buyers looking for a potentially straight-forward purchase. The accommodation comprises of a sitting room, dining area, separate kitchen, conservatory and a garage on the ground floor along with three bedrooms and a bathroom on the first floor. A particularly useful addition is the conservatory, creating an additional reception space and an ideal spot to relax and enjoy the garden throughout the seasons. To the outside, the property benefits from both front and rear gardens. The sizeable front garden is predominantly laid to lawn, providing an attractive approach to the property, whilst the enclosed rear garden offers a pleasant outdoor space for relaxing, gardening or entertaining. A garage and driveway provide convenient off-road parking and additional storage. Combining spacious accommodation, attractive gardens, a garage and driveway parking with an enviable village location close to the Cornish coastline, this property offers an excellent opportunity to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle in one of Cornwall's most desirable locations. An early viewing is strongly recommended. Colroger Close is situated within the popular and well established village of Mullion - one of the largest and most sought-after villages on the beautiful Lizard Peninsula in South Cornwall. Offering a wonderful balance of village convenience, community atmosphere and access to the spectacular Cornish coastline, Mullion is an excellent location for those looking to enjoy a relaxed coastal lifestyle. The village itself offers a good range of everyday amenities, including local shops, convenience stores, cafés, traditional Public Houses, restaurants and independent businesses. There are also primary and secondary schooling facilities, a health centre and pharmacy together with a variety of community groups and recreational activities. A particular attraction of the area is its beautiful surrounding coastline, with miles of scenic coastal walks and an abundance of picturesque beaches and secluded coves close by. Mullion Cove is a charming historic harbour, cared for by the National Trust, nestled beneath rugged cliffs and offering wonderful coastal scenery. Nearby Polurrian Cove and Poldhu Cove are particularly popular, with sandy beaches, opportunities for surfing, swimming and coastal walks along the renowned South West Coast Path. For a wider range of retail, leisure and commercial facilities, the nearby market town of Helston is approximately five miles distant, offering supermarkets, high street retailers, restaurants, leisure facilities and further schooling options. The location also provides a convenient base for exploring the wider Lizard Peninsula, including its picturesque villages, unspoilt countryside and renowned beauty spots. Combining excellent village amenities with easy access to some of Cornwall's finest beaches and coastal scenery, Mullion remains a particularly desirable location for families, retirees and those looking to embrace the very best of coastal living. text: £900,000 - £950,000. Hampstead Road, Brighton | Substantial Five-Bedroom Victorian Family Home with Versatile Living Space and Landscaped Garden. text: Set back from the road and approached via a private drive, discreetly screened by an attractive flint wall, this exceptional semi-detached home occupies a generous plot with truly remarkable far reaching field views to both the front and rear. Enjoying an enviable position within the highly sought after coastal village of Cley-next-the-Sea, the property combines charm, character and potential, with outlooks that stretch across open countryside and, to the front, take in the striking sight of two churches on the horizon. The approach is equally appealing, with a gravel driveway providing ample off road parking alongside a neatly enclosed lawned garden, leading to a welcoming entrance. The picturesque village of Cley-next-the-Sea is one of North Norfolk`s most iconic coastal locations, renowned for its rich history, charming flint cottages and thriving artistic community. Once a busy medieval port, Cley retains a strong sense of heritage, reflected in landmarks such as the historic Cley Windmill and the beautiful St Margaret`s Church, Cley. Today, it is highly regarded for its unspoilt character and relaxed coastal lifestyle. Amenities, History & Surrounding Area:. Cley offers a selection of boutique amenities including galleries, a village store, delicatessen and highly regarded places to eat, all contributing to its unique appeal. The surrounding marshes form part of the Cley Marshes Nature Reserve, one of the country`s most celebrated wildlife habitats, attracting birdwatchers and nature lovers alike. The wider coastline provides an array of scenic walks and beaches, while the nearby Georgian town of Holt offers further shopping, dining and schooling options. The village itself benefits from a strong community feel, with three churches in the wider setting and popular local pubs including the The Wiveton Bell and The Three Swallows both within walking distance. Welcome… . Old Hall stands as a magnificent Grade II listed property, rich with history and brimming with character. As the current owners prepare to move on, a rare opportunity arises for a discerning buyer to become the next custodian of this remarkable home. Poised at the edge of Gayle, Old Hall welcomes visitors with its ornate moulded doorway, inscribed with the initials MAW, marking its 1695 origins and original owner, Matthew Weatherald. Mullioned windows add to the charm of this historic residence. Come on in… Step inside to a welcoming vestibule, its tiled floor and inset stone shelves perfectly suited for shedding muddy boots after a walk on the fells. The inner hallway stretches towards the rear of the property, awash with natural light from a window at its far end. To the right, a utility storage room features original stone shelving and a rugged stone-flagged floor. Continuing down the hallway, you’ll find the bathroom, thoughtfully appointed with a bath, separate shower, washbasin, and WC. This tranquil space offers a place to relax after days spent exploring the Dales. Lovely Living Spaces… The reception rooms grace the front of the property, where deep-set windows provide inviting perches to gaze out at the world beyond. The dining room has a beamed ceiling and elegant oak herringbone floors, offering ample space for a grand dining table fit for festive gatherings. Picture magical Christmas celebrations, with loved ones gathered around, savouring the year's most anticipated meal. A striking feature fireplace, flanked by built-in cupboards, anchors the room with character. The expansive living room centres on an impressive inglenook fireplace, where the wood-burning stove takes centre stage. Beamed ceilings and twin windows with inset seats overlook the front, creating a serene spot to unwind. Envision cosy winter evenings, curled up with a film or a good book by the roaring fire. Heart of the home… The kitchen, nestled at the rear of the property, opens directly to the garden. Traditional stone flags pave the floor, while shaker-style units with pristine white worktops offer abundant storage and workspace for culinary creativity. An inset porcelain Belfast sink adds a touch of rustic charm, and there's ample space for a range-style cooker. The breakfast bar offers a relaxed setting for morning coffee or casual conversation as meals are prepared. Beyond the kitchen lies a generous walk-in pantry with original stone shelving, a haven for the home cook. From here, a staircase leads to a practical first-floor storage area. Time for bed… Ascend the original stone staircase to the first floor, where four bedrooms await. The principal bedroom is generously proportioned and features two front-facing windows and a beamed ceiling. Off the landing, a door opens to a spacious storage area tucked beneath the eaves, with a second door providing access to steps leading down to the pantry below. The second bedroom features exposed ceiling beams and dual front-facing windows, one with a delightful arch that adds a unique touch of period character. A contemporary shower room features a walk-in cubicle clad in classic white metro tiles, inset shelving for toiletries, a sleek washbasin, and a WC. The design combines modern convenience with timeless style. Further along the corridor are two additional bedrooms, presently serving as separate study spaces. The smaller of the pair is distinguished by enchanting arched, mullioned windows, a subtle homage to the property’s heritage. Outside Step out through the kitchen's rear door into a private passageway, where an outdoor store leads to a secluded, sheltered courtyard. This tranquil oasis is perfect for morning coffee, with birdsong and the soothing sounds of a nearby waterfall. Stone steps lead up to a raised patio, ideal for alfresco dining, with space for a table and chairs. Two small outbuildings on the side of the property provide storage for coal and logs. The lawn rises gently behind the house, culminating at a vantage point from which the fells unfold over the rooftops. There is space to park a car at the front of the property, with additional parking available in the village. Out and about Gayle is a picturesque village on the outskirts of Hawes, where traditional stone cottages line the banks of Gayle Beck. The beck cascades through the heart of the village in a series of gentle waterfalls, flowing toward the landmark Gayle Mill and the distinctive pepperpot silhouette of Hawes church tower on the horizon. The recently restored mill stands as a testament to the village’s rich textile heritage, and many local homes were originally built for the workers who supported that legacy. Much of the village remains unchanged, preserving a timeless quality that makes it unique. As local historians Ella Pontefract and Marie Hartley observed, "Qualities which make for quaintness: hills rising above it, houses grouped around the beck, narrow alleys, a bridge, a mill, each so perfectly placed that a first view is startling." Few are as fortunate as those who can call this enchanting village their home. A Magnificent Home Filled With Character. Built In 1695 and Steeped In History. Quaint Village Location On The Outskirts Of Hawes. Spacious Living Rooms With Beamed Ceilings & Window Seats Overlooking The Village. While Away Days With The Sound Of The Nearby Waterfall An Ever-Present Background. 4 Beautiful Bedrooms. 2 Bathrooms. Lovely Kitchen With Separate Pantry. Tiered Gardens With Seating Areas, Lawn & 3 Outbuildings For Storage

Available chain-free,14 Cornwell Road is a contemporary townhouse in Trumpington with a distinctive arrangement of space. Set over three levels, the house combines four-bedroom flexibility with a notably generous living area, while the principal bedroom occupies the top floor with direct access onto a large private terrace. The main living and dining room is particularly successful. A double-height section featuring a mezzanine balcony and substantial roof glazing giving the room a sense of volume and bringing natural light deep into the house, while glazed doors open directly onto the attractive rear garden. There is ample space to accommodate distinct sitting and dining areas without either feeling compromised, providing a picturesque outlook onto the rear garden. The kitchen is separate and practical, with a broad run of fitted cabinetry, extensive quartz work surfaces and integrated appliances. The ground floor space is completed by under-stairs storage and a separate cloakroom. The bedroom accommodation is spread through the upper floors, creating useful separation from the main living space. The principal bedroom has the top floor to itself, with a distinct dressing area, en suite shower room and opening directly onto the substantial terrace, providing a private outside space that is a genuine additional feature of the house. On the first floor, there are a further two double bedrooms one with its own en-suite shower room and the other with access to the main bathroom, while the fourth bedroom is currently arranged as a study with a sliding door to the mezzanine balcony that overlooks the ground-floor living room below, demonstrating how readily the layout accommodates regular home working without taking over the living areas. Outside, the attractive enclosed rear garden has been designed to be relatively easy to maintain, with gravelled areas, established planting and space for outdoor dining. Parking is another practical strength, with both a garage and carport providing considerably more flexibility than is often available with modern Cambridge housing. Trumpington works particularly well for those who need straightforward access into Cambridge, the Biomedical Campus, the wider road network or trains into central London. Cornwell Road is within the established Great Kneighton area, with cycling routes and the Guided Busway providing useful alternatives to the car, while nearby green spaces give this part of south Cambridge a welcome sense of openness. Situated roughly a quarter of a mile from the Addenbrooke's Hospital / Cambridge Biomedical Campus, this property sits just a 12 minute walk, via Hobson Avenue, from the new Cambridge South railway station with, at peak travel times, up to nine trains every hour to central London stations. 120 sqm / 1293 sqf. 161 sqm / 0.04 acre. text: Tucked away in an elevated position with a peaceful Lakeland hamlet, Bigert Mire Cottage is an attractive, traditional three bedroom detached property offering an exceptional blend of timeless charm and breathtaking natural beauty. With spectacular, far-reaching views across the Duddon Valley. The property is extremely well proportioned and well presented benefiting from many original features including exposed beam, spiral stone staircase, latched doors together with modern appointments including underfloor heating. The property has two reception rooms with the open plan living/kitchen/diner and benefiting from a secondary lounge/dining room. Additionally the ground floor it has a highly useful multifunctional room primarily used as a utility room/boot room/office with adjoining cloakroom. The first floor has three bedrooms of which two are spacious doubles and the third is a single bunk room. All three rooms take advantage of the superb panoramic fells and country views. Detached from the cottage is a paddock and delightful enclosed garden, with the benefit of splendid views of the valley. There is a parking space next to the gable end and parking is also available within the paddock area. The Duddon Valley is a beautiful and peaceful unspoilt area in the southwest corner of the Lake District National Park. It is set amongst the beautiful Furness Fells and close to the picturesque village of Broughton (3 miles), voted village of the year 2002, and the market town of Ulverston. Good road links via the A595 and A590 trunk road connect it to the M6 Barrow-in-Furness and north to Scotland. The valley can also be approached from the heart of the National Park either from Coniston (10 miles) Ambleside (18 miles) and the central passes of Hard Knott and Wrynose. Internal viewing is essential to fully appreciate its unique atmosphere and unmatched setting. Accommodation. Three Hollies occupies a rare position where privacy and connection exist in perfect balance. Here, mornings begin with birdsong drifting through open windows, evenings soften beneath golden western light, and every season leaves its own distinct mark upon the landscape beyond. Approached along a peaceful residential lane lined with mature trees and established homes, the first impression is one of quiet elegance. Gardens rich with greenery frame the house beautifully, softening the stone and drawing the eye towards glimpses of distant fells and the lake beyond. There is nothing hurried about this setting. Everything feels settled, grounded and wonderfully timeless. Over the years, the house has evolved carefully and naturally, growing into the warm and versatile home it is today. Original character remains woven throughout, while thoughtful additions have introduced a gentler openness to the flow of everyday life. The result is a home that feels both generous and deeply welcoming, with each space unfolding easily into the next. At its heart lies the kitchen and dining space, filled with natural light and connected beautifully to the gardens outside. It is easy to imagine long breakfasts here as sunlight pours across the table, or evenings gathered with friends after days spent on the water or walking the surrounding fells. During warmer months, doors open naturally onto the garden, allowing inside and outside living to blend effortlessly together. Elsewhere, quieter corners provide places to retreat and unwind. The sitting room feels particularly inviting, with broad windows framing the greenery outside and evening light stretching softly across the room as the day fades. There is a warmth here that feels unmistakably Lakeland. Cosy during winter storms, calm and airy through summer, and always connected to the changing colours and moods of the landscape beyond. Additional living spaces offer flexibility for modern family life. A snug for quieter evenings, a study overlooking the gardens, perhaps a creative space or reading room. The beauty of the layout lies in its adaptability, allowing the home to evolve naturally around the lives lived within it. Upstairs, four beautifully proportioned bedrooms continue the same atmosphere of light and tranquillity. Some gaze out towards distant fells, others across mature trees and gardens that shift gently with the seasons. Morning mist rising beyond the rooftops, autumn colour settling into the surrounding woodland, soft winter frost catching the first light. Every window seems to frame a different moment of the Lake District landscape. The bedrooms themselves feel restful and calm, removed from the pace of everyday life below. Two bathrooms serve the accommodation with ease, making the house equally suited to family living, visiting guests or long weekends shared with friends. Outside, the gardens are wonderfully established and deeply private. Mature planting creates shelter and softness throughout, while open lawns and quiet seating areas invite slow afternoons spent outdoors. There are spaces to follow the sun throughout the day, from peaceful morning coffee beneath the trees to long summer evenings watching the light fade slowly behind the western horizon. The west-facing aspect gives the house a particularly beautiful quality as evening approaches. Golden light spills across the gardens and into the living spaces, while the surrounding landscape takes on the soft glow so characteristic of the Lakes at dusk. It is a home that feels closely tied to the rhythm of nature and the passing of the seasons. Ferney Green itself remains one of Bowness-on-Windermere's most quietly desirable settings. Tucked away from the busiest stretches of the village, it carries a far more residential and peaceful atmosphere, where homes are often held for generations and neighbours know one another by name. Yet despite its calm surroundings, the heart of Bowness remains within easy reach. Independent cafés, elegant restaurants and welcoming pubs line the village streets, while the shores of Lake Windermere offer sailing, paddleboarding and lakeside walks throughout the year. Nearby Windermere village provides further amenities and rail connections, linking the area seamlessly with the wider country while allowing daily life here to feel beautifully detached from it all. For those drawn outdoors, the surrounding landscape offers endless opportunity. Walks begin directly from the doorstep, winding through woodland paths, climbing nearby viewpoints or following quiet lanes towards the water's edge. Days can be spent exploring the central fells, returning home to warmth, stillness and the gentle glow of evening light settling across the garden. The home benefits from a versatile garage currently used as a gym, along with a separate carport providing additional covered parking. At the bottom of the garden there is further parking space for two cars, offering excellent off-road capacity. The sale also includes two garden sheds, which will remain and provide useful outdoor storage. What makes Three Hollies so special is not simply its location or its proportions, but the feeling it creates from the moment you arrive. There is a softness to the atmosphere here. A sense of ease. The kind of home where family gathers naturally, where weekends stretch longer than expected, and where ordinary moments feel quietly elevated by the beauty of the surroundings. It is a place equally suited to permanent living or cherished escapes to the Lakes. Somewhere to celebrate Christmas beside the fire, to host summer lunches spilling into the garden, or simply to step away from the pace of modern life and reconnect with quieter things. In a part of the Lake District where privacy, character and setting are increasingly difficult to find together, Three Hollies offers something deeply special. For a residential buyer, there is plenty of scope to return these rooms into reception rooms or office space to create a generous family home. At the front the bay-windowed room is the largest of the ground-floor spaces and would make an excellent main sitting room. Behind this is another separate room which could work particularly well as a dining room, snug, playroom or home office. The kitchen runs out from the rear of the house and is fitted with a long run of white units and plenty of worktop space. There is room for informal seating alongside, while windows to the side and rear bring in good natural light and a door leads directly out to the garden. There is also a toilet under the stairs. The first floor has three bedrooms. The larger rooms have retained their original timber floorboards and benefit from good ceiling heights, while the front bedroom is a particularly impressive space with a wide bay window spanning much of the front elevation. The third room works well as a single bedroom, nursery or study. A spacious family bathroom also sits on this floor, fitted with a bath and overhead shower. The top floor provides another generous double bedroom, naturally lit by two velux windows and set apart from the rest of the house. An additional shower room on this level makes it particularly useful as a main bedroom, guest suite or space for an older child. Overall, the layout gives a new owner plenty of options and the property is offered with no onward chain. Outside space. text: A charming and deceptively spacious three-bedroom terraced home, ideally positioned in the heart of Horsforth, just a short walk from the vibrant amenities of Town Street. Arranged over three floors, with a useful cellar, this characterful property combines generous accommodation with attractive period features, including tall ceilings, exposed timber flooring, an impressive cast iron fireplace and exposed stonework. The property offers two well-proportioned double bedrooms, a superb top-floor principal bedroom, a welcoming sitting room, a fitted kitchen and a traditional house bathroom. Externally, there is a low-maintenance courtyard-style garden to the front, off-street parking for one vehicle to the rear and additional permit parking available on the street. An appealing home in a highly convenient location, ideal for those seeking character, space and easy access to local amenities. LOCATION . Horsforth, named as one of the top 10 most desirable postcodes in England and is a prime residential location, popular with families and young professionals alike. The property is within easy reach of an array of excellent amenities including well regarded schooling for all ages, lovely canal & river walks, and the extensive shopping facilities found on New Road Side and Town Street including Morrisons supermarket. Horsforth Hall Park is a great addition to the community with a children’s playground, bandstand, cricket pitch, skate park and bowling green. For commuters, Horsforth Train Station provides services to Leeds, York and Harrogate. Kirkstall Forge Train Station is located down the A65 and offers further means of convenient access into the city (8 mins) and surrounding areas. The Ring Road (A6120) and the (A65) are nearby and provide main road links to the commercial centres of Leeds, Bradford, York and Harrogate, a regular bus service runs into the City Centre and, for the more travelled commuter, Leeds-Bradford Airport is a short drive away. All in all, this location is sought after by a wide variety of buyers and enjoys a strong sense of community and a thriving village atmosphere. GROUND FLOOR . The property opens directly into a spacious and welcoming sitting room, where tall ceilings and a large front-facing window create a wonderful sense of space and natural light. An impressive cast iron fireplace, complete with timber and tiled surround and a gas and coal-effect fire, provides an attractive focal point, enhancing the room’s period charm. Stairs rise to the first floor, while the kitchen is positioned to the rear and is fitted with a range of wall and base units, with space for freestanding appliances. A rear door provides access outside, and a further staircase leads down to the cellar. Exposed stonework alongside the cellar steps adds a distinctive character feature to the kitchen. CELLAR . A generously proportioned and versatile cellar provides excellent additional storage, benefiting from power, windows to both the front and rear, good head height and natural light. Offering potential for a variety of uses or possible conversion, subject to the necessary consents, this useful space adds further flexibility to the property. FIRST FLOOR . The first floor continues the home’s character, with exposed timber flooring extending across the landing and into two well-proportioned double bedrooms, positioned to the front and rear respectively. Both rooms are neutrally decorated and offer comfortable accommodation. Completing this level is the traditional three-piece house bathroom, comprising a bath with shower over, pedestal wash basin and WC, complemented by part-white ceramic tiling. A useful fitted storage cupboard off the landing provides additional practicality. SECOND FLOOR . Occupying the entire top floor is an impressive and private principal bedroom. This well-proportioned, dual-aspect room benefits from dormer windows to both the front and rear, creating generous head height and allowing plenty of natural light to fill the space. Complemented by fitted furniture, the bedroom offers a comfortable and private retreat, completing the accommodation beautifully. OUTSIDE . To the front, a paved courtyard-style garden provides a pleasant, low-maintenance outdoor space with room for potted plants, seating and hanging washing. An exceptional three/four bedroom detached family home situated within a cul-de-sac location with versatile accommodation and generous gardens. DESCRIPTION. Occupying a desirable cul-de-sac position on the edge of the popular Moorhayes development, 10 Honeysuckle Close is a beautifully presented three/four-bedroom detached family home offering generous and versatile living accommodation, driveway parking for three cars and attractive enclosed gardens. Previously configured as a four-bedroom property, the former owners have combined Bedrooms 3 and 4 to create an impressive guest bedroom, although the original layout could be easily reinstated to suit growing families. The property benefits from a substantial sitting room, created from the former double garage, with potential for a first-floor extension above, subject to the necessary planning consents. The accommodation is both spacious and flexible, with a useful porch leading you to the welcoming entrance hall with access to a cloakroom, fitted with WC, wash hand basin and heated towel rail and storage cupboard with radiator perfect for drying clothes. To the front of the property, the dining room enjoys a bay window and feature fireplace, creating an ideal setting for formal dining. The heart of the home is the impressive kitchen/breakfast room, enjoying views over the rear garden and fitted with an extensive range of matching wall and base units, complemented by a central island with electric sockets, wine rack, additional storage and breakfast bar seating. Integrated appliances include a fridge/freezer and dishwasher, while there is space for a range cooker. The adjoining breakfast area offers plenty of room for everyday dining. Leading from the kitchen is a well-equipped utility room with further storage, space and plumbing for laundry appliances, and direct access to the garden through french doors. The standout feature of the property is the superb sitting room. Converted from the original double garage, this reception space offers generous proportions, a feature electric fireplace, and French doors opening onto the rear garden. In addition, the summer room provides a versatile and light-filled space, overlooking the gardens and benefitting from two sets of sliding doors, making it ideal as a family room, garden room, or entertaining area. On the first floor, the spacious principal bedroom enjoys a front aspect, fitted wardrobes, and an en-suite shower room with shower, WC, wash hand basin and heated towel rail. Bedroom Two is a comfortable double room with fitted wardrobes and a rear outlook. Bedroom Three has been enlarged by combining two bedrooms and now offers a substantial double room with fitted wardrobes and views over the rear garden. The family bathroom is fitted with a modern suite comprising a freestanding bath with shower attachment, WC, wash hand basin and heated towel rail. From the first floor landing the loft can be accessed, which is boarded with ladder lighting and power sockets. SITUATION. The property is situated in the popular residential area known as Moorhayes on the edge of Tiverton with a small range of shops including Tesco Express. Tiverton provides an excellent range of shopping, banking, recreational healthcare and educational facilities. Easy commuting via the North Devon Link Road either to the north coast via Barnstaple or eastward back to the M5 (J27) and Parkway mainline railway station. Exeter lies some 18 miles to the south and offers a more comprehensive range of facilities as befitting a Cathedral City and Taunton, the County Town of Somerset lies approximately 19 miles to the north, again offering a varied and comprehensive range of facilities. OUTSIDE . To the front of the property, a private driveway provides off-road parking for numerous vehicles and benefits from an EV charging point. The front garden has been designed for ease of maintenance, with a combination of paving, decorative chippings, and established shrubs. Useful storage areas that run the full length of both sides the property with light and power. The enclosed rear garden provides a wonderful outdoor space for families and entertaining alike. Predominantly laid to lawn, with raised planted borders and vegetable patch, it also features an elevated composite decking area ideal for al fresco dining and summer gatherings. Completing the garden is an attractive summerhouse which is currently used as a gym, it comes with electric lighting, electric heating, TV aerial and WIFI. with adjoining wooden pergola, creating the perfect spot to relax and enjoy the surroundings. Plot 25, The Daisy, has been designed for effortless, modern single-storey living. The welcoming entrance hall sets the tone for a home that feels immediately light, confortable and beautifully proportioned. At its heart lies the impressive 27ft x 13ft kitchen/living/dining room, a wonderfully sociable space flooded with natural light from the windows and full-height glazed double doors that open directly onto the rear garden. This seamless connection between inside and out creates a home that feels open in the summer months and cosy in the winter – perfect for relaxed breakfasts, family meals or entertaining friends. The contemporary kitchen offers generous storage and integrated appliances and there is further direct garden access from the kitchen area as well. The bedrooms are equally well considered. A generous second double bedroom ensures guests can stay in comfort or this space could be used for alternative purposes – ideal as a home office or hobby room perhpas. Outside, the bungalow occupies a good sized plot, perfect for those seeking manageable yet enjoyable outdoor space. Whether it’s a sunny morning coffee on the patio, light gardening, or simply relaxing in the fresh Devon air, the garden complements the easy-living design of the home. An attractively planted front lawn and flowerbeds enhance the kerb appeal, while the garage together with an additional 2 parking sapces provides practicality and security that many buyers now consider essential. Nestled on the eastern bank of the Torridge estuary in the historic village of East-the-Water on the fringes of the market town of Bideford, Chapel Green is the latest lifestyle-led development of just 26 high-quality homes by award-winning Baker Estates. This carefully considered scheme has just been released, and as a smaller, more selct development, it is already attracting interest from those seeking easy, modern living in beautiful North Devon. This new neigbourhood will comprise a mixture of single-storey bungalows as well a two-storey chalet style homes, arranged around a quiet cul-de-sac. East-the-Water village sits five miles upriver from the open sea and still retains a friendly, close-knit feel with its own doctor’s surgery and onsite pharmacy, a Tesco supermarket and highly rated Spar store, local pubs and takeaways, and even allotments. Across Bideford’s ancient Long Bridge lie further amenities such as the library, arts centre, Pannier market and retail outlets, while regular buses connect East-the-Water to Barnstaple, Westward Ho! and Appledore. Chapel Green is perfectly placed for tranquil village living with easy access to this array of coastal, countryside and market-town attractions. The development comprises three home types: The Primrose, a spacious three-bedroom detached bungalow with two bathrooms; The Holly, a generous three-bedroom chalet bungalow with living space arranged over two floors; and The Daisy, a low-maintenance two-bedroom bungalow ideal for those seeking simplicity. Most properties benefit from either a single or double garage, and some include a car port; every plot has additional driveway parking. Gardens are generous yet manageable—ideal for morning coffee on the patio, gentle gardening or simply enjoying the fresh Devon air. Internally, these homes are designed for contemporary comfort: chic kitchens feature built-in appliances, and bathrooms are fitted with stylish sanitary ware and tiling. Light oak-veneer internal doors, gas-fired central heating and uPVC double glazing create warmth and low maintenance. Energy efficiency has been prioritised to keep running costs low, and every property is backed by a 10-year NHBC warranty for peace of mind. Baker Estates’ Moving Made Easy suite includes home exchange and assisted move schemes, lifetime mortgage options for over-55s, and attractive packages for armed forces and key workers, with introductions to independent financial advisers available. As well as the local facilities, there is plenty to explore further afield. Barnstaple, North Devon’s largest town, is only about seven miles away. It grew at the lowest crossing of the River Taw and today offers the region’s main shopping centre, markets and rail station. To the north, the old fishing village of Appledore lies at the mouth of the River Torridge just three miles from Bideford; it has a rich maritime heritage and is about six miles west of Barnstaple. Across the estuary, the quaint village of Instow sits where the rivers Taw and Torridge meet; it boasts a sandy beach, sand dunes with rare orchids and is served by the Tarka Trail and South West Coast Path. For beach lovers, Westward Ho! offers two miles of Blue Flag sand backed by a unique pebble ridge and Northam Burrows Country Park, while the nearby surfing beaches at Saunton, Croyde, Putsborough and Woolacombe form part of the North Devon World Surfing Reserve, a 30 km stretch of coastline renowned for its consistent, world-class waves. The South West Coast Path itself runs for 630 miles along the peninsula; from Exmoor to Cornwall it provides spectacular scenery and nourishment for mind, body and soul. Exmoor National Park and the wild open moorland beyond offer further walking, cycling and wildlife-watching opportunities. Thalassa is a delightful cottage occupying a lovely position along Gabber Lane, in the sought-after coastal village of Down Thomas. Combining traditional charm with surprisingly spacious accommodation, the property enjoys a wonderful setting with beautiful countryside surroundings and distant coastal views, making it an ideal home for those seeking a quieter pace of life whilst remaining within easy reach of Plymouth and local amenities. The accommodation begins with a spacious entrance reception room, offering a versatile area that could easily be used as a home office or study, ideal for those working from home. An opening leads through to the comfortable lounge, a welcoming room with a feature fireplace housing a fitted log-burning stove, creating a lovely focal point and a cosy atmosphere during the colder months. From the lounge, an opening leads into a generously proportioned kitchen/dining room, fitted with a range of units providing useful storage and worktop space, together with ample room for a dining table. The kitchen also provides access to the rear garden, whilst a staircase rises to the first-floor accommodation. On the first floor are two well-proportioned double bedrooms, offering comfortable accommodation and enjoying the benefits of the property's attractive surroundings. A shower room, fitted with a three-piece suite, completes the first-floor accommodation. The front garden is particularly appealing, with a variety of established flowering shrubs, bushes and mature planting creating an attractive outdoor space. A seating area provides a wonderful spot to sit and relax whilst taking in the lovely views across the surrounding fields and countryside. To the rear is a delightful mature garden, predominantly laid to lawn and complemented by established planting. A timber-built summerhouse provides a lovely additional feature, offering a peaceful place to enjoy the garden or useful space for hobbies and relaxation. Offered for sale with vacant possession and no onward chain, the property would make an ideal permanent residence, coastal retreat or home for those looking to enjoy village life within easy reach of the South Devon coastline. Down Thomas is a picturesque and highly regarded village situated on the beautiful South Devon coastline, approximately six miles from Plymouth city centre. Surrounded by rolling countryside and close to the coast, the village offers a peaceful rural atmosphere whilst remaining conveniently positioned for the everyday amenities available in nearby Heybrook Bay, Staddiscombe, Elburton and Plymstock. The surrounding area is particularly popular with walkers and outdoor enthusiasts, with access to scenic coastal paths, beautiful countryside walks and nearby beaches, including Wembury and Bovisand. Plymstock provides a wider range of amenities, including supermarkets, independent shops, cafés, healthcare facilities and schools, whilst Plymouth city centre offers an extensive selection of shopping, leisure and transport facilities. The location offers an excellent balance of village tranquillity, beautiful natural surroundings and access to the wider Plymouth area. Charming Two-Bedroom Coastal Cottage. Generous Kitchen/Dining Room. Two Well-Proportioned Double Bedrooms. Attractive Front & Rear Gardens. Mature Rear Garden with Timber Summerhouse. Vacant Possession & No Onward Chain

Full of character, charm and generous living space, this substantial period home offers a wonderful combination of elegant original features, versatile accommodation and a genuinely welcoming neighbourhood. Situated on a street renowned for its friendly neighbours and lively community spirit, the property is just a 30-second walk from the beautiful Devonport Park, making it an exceptional place to call home. From the moment you step inside, the house reveals the proportions and architectural charm that make period properties so desirable. High ceilings, ornate ceiling roses and a wealth of period features create a wonderful sense of character throughout, while the spacious rooms provide plenty of flexibility for modern family life. The ground floor offers an excellent balance of everyday living and entertaining space. To the front of the property, the generously proportioned lounge provides an inviting place to relax, with its period detailing adding a sense of elegance and warmth. Beyond this, the separate dining room is equally impressive, offering ample space for family meals, dinner parties and special occasions. To the rear, the substantial kitchen and breakfast room forms the heart of the home, with plenty of room for cooking, informal dining and gathering together. A convenient ground-floor WC completes the accommodation on this level. The sense of space continues upstairs, where the first floor is home to an exceptionally generous principal bedroom, a large family bathroom and a further spacious room currently arranged as a study. There is an additional wonderfully versatile room could equally serve as an additional bedroom/craft room, depending on the needs of its next owners. The family bathroom is particularly impressive in its proportions, offering a level of space rarely found in more modern homes. The second floor provides three further bedrooms, together with an additional bathroom, creating a flexible arrangement that lends itself beautifully to family living, visiting guests or working from home. With accommodation extending across four floors, including a substantial cellar divided into three useful areas, there is an abundance of space for storage, hobbies and the changing demands of everyday life. Outside, the property continues to impress with a south-facing courtyard garden, a lovely spot to enjoy the sunshine, dine outdoors or unwind with a morning coffee. The courtyard offers a manageable outdoor space without the demands of a larger garden, while the added benefit of off-road parking, accessed via a roller door, is a particularly valuable feature. What makes this home especially appealing, however, is not simply the house itself but the lifestyle that comes with it. The street has a wonderful reputation for its friendly neighbours and strong sense of community, with celebrations and street parties bringing residents together and creating the sort of atmosphere that is increasingly difficult to find. It is a place where neighbours know one another and where a genuine sense of belonging forms part of everyday life. And with Devonport Park just 30 seconds away on foot, one of the area's most treasured green spaces is practically on the doorstep. Whether it's a morning stroll, time spent outdoors with the family or simply enjoying a little peace and greenery, the park feels like a natural extension of home. Offering approximately 2,849 sq. ft. of accommodation, including the cellar, this is a home of impressive proportions, rich period character and remarkable versatility. Combining beautiful architectural details, generous rooms, practical features and a truly special community setting, it presents a rare opportunity to enjoy the charm of a traditional period property alongside the comforts and convenience of modern living. Substantial Period Family Home. Approximately 2,849 Sq. Ft. Including Cellar. Four/Five Spacious Bedrooms. Wealth of Original Period Features. High Ceilings & Ornate Ceiling Roses. Generous Lounge & Separate Dining Room. Spacious Kitchen/Breakfast Room. Two Bathrooms & Ground Floor WC. South-Facing Courtyard Garden & Off-Road Parking. Just Moments from Devonport Park

Cadgwith has its origins in medieval times as a collection of fish cellars in a sheltered south east facing coastal valley with a shingle cove. Fishing subsidised local farmers' livelihoods. From the 16th Century the village became inhabited with fishing as the main occupation. Subsequently houses, lofts, capstan houses and cellars, constructed of local stone or cob walls and thatched or slated roofs, were built along the beach and up the sides of the valley leading to Cadgwith's characteristic Cornish fishing village appearance. In recent times a very small Anglican Church was built dedicated to St Mary. Today Cadgwith functions as a small fishing cove with fishermen seen bringing in their haul and working on their boats. Also the Cove has an extremely popular public house which is home to the famous Cadgwith Singers, who are well known for their repertoire of traditional folk songs. For day to day needs the close by village of Ruan Minor boasts an active community with many clubs, societies and organisations, primary school, local store/post office, Anglican Church, Methodist Chapel and doctor's surgery. Cadgwith Cove is often used as a filming location such as fisherman's apprentice, Harry Potter and just recently Hercules Pirot. In the area is the National Trust's picturesque Kynance Cove, the village of The Lizard, which is mainland Britain's most Southerly Point and the stretches of golden sands at Kennack. Comprehensive schooling is available in the nearby village of Mullion, which lies approximately four miles distant, where there is a doctors' surgery, pharmacy and a good selection of shops. The market town of Helston is approximately ten miles away and includes a good range of amenities having a sports centre with indoor swimming pool and a variety of national shops and supermarkets. text: Situated just a four or five-minute walk from Broadway’s picturesque High Street, this well-positioned two-bedroom mid-terrace home offers an excellent opportunity for first-time buyers, downsizers or those seeking a conveniently located Cotswold bolthole. Offering approximately 600 sq ft of accommodation, the property comprises a welcoming reception room to the front, a kitchen to the rear, two bedrooms and a family bathroom. Location – Broadway, Worcestershire Often referred to as the ‘Jewel of the Cotswolds’, Broadway is one of the region’s most recognisable and sought-after villages, celebrated for its beautiful honey-coloured Cotswold stone buildings, wide, tree-lined High Street and exceptional setting beneath the Cotswold escarpment. The village offers a wonderful blend of traditional charm and everyday convenience, with an excellent selection of independent boutiques, delicatessens, cafés, restaurants and traditional country pubs. Notable destinations include The Lygon Arms, a historic coaching inn at the heart of the village, alongside a variety of galleries, antique shops and independent retailers. For those who enjoy the outdoors, Broadway is surrounded by some of the Cotswolds’ finest countryside, with an extensive network of public footpaths and bridleways, including the Cotswold Way National Trail. The iconic Broadway Tower, perched high above the village, provides spectacular panoramic views across the surrounding countryside. Despite its peaceful rural setting, Broadway is well connected to the wider region. The nearby towns of Evesham, Chipping Campden and Moreton-in-Marsh offer additional amenities, while mainline railway services from Evesham and Moreton-in-Marsh provide connections towards Worcester, Oxford and London Paddington. The A44 also offers convenient road access to the surrounding towns and villages. Combining an enviable village location with manageable accommodation, private parking and the convenience of being within easy walking distance of Broadway’s many attractions, this property represents an appealing opportunity in one of the Cotswolds’ most desirable locations. text: A charming two-bedroom period home in a sought-after position on Bath’s northern slopes, with practical accommodation and a garden. If you're looking for your first home and want somewhere you can quite comfortably move straight into without having a long list of jobs to do, then this could be a great option for you. Situated on Limestone Close in Great Blakenham, this property has been owned by the current owners from new, and they've done a lovely job of looking after it. It's fresh, modern and well presented throughout, with some lovely additions, including decorative wall panelling, updated flooring and landscaping to both the front and rear of the property. One of the things that sets this house apart from many similar properties is the addition of a really good-sized garage that comfortably fits a large car. Alongside the nicely paved frontage, driveway parking and EV charging point, you've got plenty of space for your parking needs. Stepping through the front door, you've got a nice entrance hallway with a downstairs WC to your left and the kitchen and dining room to your right. It's a nicely proportioned kitchen, with plenty of worktop and cupboard space whilst still allowing enough room to comfortably sit down and enjoy dinner together. To the rear of the property is the living room. Spanning the full width of the house, it's a lovely space to get comfortable on the sofa at the end of the day. The French doors allow plenty of natural light into the room and, throughout the summer months, it's nice to be able to open these up and make the most of the garden. Upstairs, there are three bedrooms and the family bathroom. The two larger bedrooms are generous doubles, with the main bedroom also benefiting from built-in storage. The third bedroom, whilst slightly smaller, currently accommodates a double bed, although it would equally work well as a nursery or a home office, depending on your needs. The rear garden is a really manageable size, with a patio area immediately outside the French doors and the remainder predominantly laid to lawn. There's enough space to enjoy having friends and family over in the summer or for the dog to run around, without having to dedicate your entire weekend to maintaining it. Thanks to the positioning of the house within the development, it also enjoys a little more privacy than you might typically expect from a property of this nature. You've got direct access into the garage from the garden, too. Whether you're using it to park the car, store your bikes and outdoor equipment or even create a little home gym, having that additional space is a real benefit. Now, one of the things I particularly like about Great Blakenham is that you get to enjoy that slightly more rural feel without having to sacrifice the convenience of having everything you need nearby. Within a couple of minutes of leaving the house, you can be on the A14, heading towards Ipswich, Stowmarket or Bury St Edmunds. Equally, you can leave the car at home and enjoy some lovely walks along the River Gipping, taking you in one direction towards Bramford Meadows and in the other towards Needham Market and its lake. It's a particularly lovely location if you've got a dog or simply enjoy getting outdoors. Within walking distance of the property, you've got a Tesco Express, an Indian restaurant, a local gym, the village hall and recreation ground. The neighbouring village of Claydon offers even more, including a Co-op, a couple of lovely local pubs in the Greyhound and the Crown, as well as local schools. For those who need to commute by train, you've also got the benefit of railway stations at both Needham Market, Ipswich and Stowmarket within driving distance. The development itself is now nicely established and, unlike some modern developments, doesn't feel overly crowded, with a good provision of parking throughout. For me, it's the combination of the condition of the house, the additional space provided by the garage and the convenience of the location that makes this such an appealing first home. Somewhere you can get the keys, get your furniture in and simply start enjoying living there. Beautifully presented & move-in ready. Ideal first-time purchase. Large garage & driveway parking. EV charging point. Spacious living room with French doors. 3 Double Bedrooms. Downstairs WC. Low-maintenance garden. Walking distance to shops & countryside walks. Excellent access to the A14

Occupying a desirable position within a quiet cul-de-sac in the popular town of Halesworth, this fully renovated detached bungalow offers stylish single-level living with the benefit of a turnkey finish throughout. Having undergone improvements including a full re-wire, re-plastering, new windows, doors, decoration and the roof has been re-done. The property also benefits from electric heating and a hot water system, with provisions in place for the future installation of solar panels if desired. The bright and airy accommodation centres around a spacious open-plan kitchen, dining and living area, flooded with natural light and ideal for modern family living or entertaining guests. Three versatile bedrooms provide flexibility for home working, hobbies or visiting family, while the contemporary shower room adds further appeal. Outside, a private and well-maintained garden, driveway parking and a detached garage complete this attractive home, making it an excellent choice for those looking to downsize without compromise. The Location Barons Close enjoys a peaceful setting on the edge of Halesworth, one of East Suffolk’s most established market towns. Well suited to families, professionals, retirees and those seeking a balance between town and countryside living, the location combines everyday convenience with easy access to the Suffolk Heritage Coast. Halesworth has retained much of its historic character, centred around the Thoroughfare, a popular pedestrianised shopping street lined with independent retailers, cafés, delicatessens and local services, creating a strong sense of community and a welcoming atmosphere. Residents benefit from supermarkets including Co-op and Morrisons, together with healthcare services, pharmacies, banking facilities and a public library. The Cut Arts Centre, housed within a converted maltings building, is a key cultural venue offering theatre productions, cinema screenings, live music and community events throughout the year. A selection of restaurants, traditional pubs and coffee shops can be found within the town centre, while nearby Beccles, Southwold and Lowestoft provide further shopping, dining and leisure opportunities. Families are well served by local education options. Halesworth Primary School and Edgar Sewter Community Primary School are both within the town, while Bungay High School and Framlingham College are among the wider schooling choices available in the surrounding area. The town’s range of educational facilities, sports clubs and community groups contributes to its appeal for households of all ages. Halesworth railway station provides regular services along the East Suffolk Line, connecting with Ipswich and Lowestoft, while onward services offer access to Norwich and London Liverpool Street. The A144 links the town with Bungay and the A12, providing straightforward road connections to the wider Suffolk and Norfolk regions. Regular bus services also connect surrounding villages and neighbouring coastal towns. Beyond the practical advantages of the town itself, the surrounding landscape is a major attraction. Halesworth sits within the Blyth Valley and is home to the Millennium Green, a substantial area of riverside meadow and walking trails close to the centre. The renowned coastal destinations of Southwold, Walberswick and Dunwich are all within easy reach, offering beaches, nature reserves and scenic walking routes. Finished in neutral décor and benefiting from the recent renovations carried out by the current owners, the hallway provides access to all principal rooms and enhances the excellent flow throughout the home. At the heart of the property lies the impressive open-plan kitchen, dining and living space, thoughtfully designed to create a sociable and versatile setting for modern living. Flooded with natural light from two front-facing windows, the living and dining area feels welcoming and spacious, providing ample room for both relaxation and entertaining. The open layout allows family and guests to interact effortlessly, whether gathering for everyday meals or larger social occasions. The kitchen forms an integral part of this space and has been fitted with a range of modern cabinetry, providing practical storage alongside contemporary styling. Well-equipped for day-to-day use, it includes an integrated oven, induction hob, sink and drainer unit, dishwasher and fridge/freezer. The layout has been carefully considered to maximise both functionality and convenience, creating a bright and efficient environment for cooking and dining. The bedroom accommodation is equally adaptable, offering three well-proportioned rooms that cater to a variety of requirements. The principal bedroom provides a comfortable and private space to unwind, while the additional bedrooms offer flexible options for visiting guests, family members or those working from home. One room could easily serve as a dedicated home office, nursery or dressing room, allowing the property to adapt as lifestyle needs change. Serving the bedrooms is a contemporary shower room, fitted with a modern three-piece suite. Stylish yet practical, the room also benefits from built-in storage solutions and a heated towel rail, ensuring both comfort and convenience while maintaining a clean and uncluttered appearance. Stepping outside, the rear garden offers a private and well-maintained outdoor space that can be enjoyed throughout the seasons. A paved patio area provides the perfect setting for outdoor seating and al fresco dining, while the generous lawn creates an attractive backdrop and space for gardening enthusiasts, visiting grandchildren or pets to enjoy. To the front, the property continues to impress with its neatly presented appearance and practical parking arrangements. The driveway provides off-road parking, while the detached single garage offers valuable storage capacity for bicycles, gardening equipment and household items. SITUATION & LOCATION This delightful newly built detached bungalow situated in the sought-after Suffolk village of Badwell Ash. Designed to provide spacious, high-specification single-storey living, the property combines contemporary energy-efficient technology with generous accommodation and attractive outdoor space. The bungalow extends to approximately 2,328 sq ft and features a thoughtfully planned layout, with the living and bedroom accommodation arranged around a central hallway, creating a clear separation between entertaining areas and private spaces. At the heart of the home is an impressive open-plan kitchen and dining area, fitted with high-quality painted Shaker-style cabinetry, quartz worktops and a full range of integrated Bosch appliances. French doors open directly onto the Indian Sandstone terrace and gardens, creating a seamless connection between indoor and outdoor living. A separate utility room provides additional storage and practicality. The spacious dual-aspect sitting room offers a welcoming focal point, featuring a brick fireplace with a wood-burning stove and French doors leading to the gardens. The accommodation comprises three generously proportioned double bedrooms, all benefiting from en suite facilities. The principal suite features a walk-in dressing room and a luxurious fully tiled en suite shower room with twin washbasins and a large walk-in shower. The second bedroom enjoys French doors opening onto the south facing garden, making it ideal for guests, while the third bedroom's Jack-and-Jill en suite shower room also serves as a convenient guest shower room off the hall. Externally, the property sits within wraparound gardens and benefits from a substantial block-paved driveway providing ample parking and turning space. A detached double garage with electric roller doors further enhances the property's practicality. Built with sustainability in mind, the bungalow benefits from an air-source heat pump, underfloor heating throughout, a 7kW solar panel system, a predicted EPC rating of A, and a 10-year structural warranty. In addition, the boarded roof space, complete with attic trusses and rooflights, provides excellent storage and offers potential for future conversion, subject to the necessary consents. In summary this is a high-quality contemporary bungalow offering spacious, energy-efficient living in a peaceful village setting, ideal for buyers seeking modern comfort, low running costs and the convenience of single-storey accommodation. The property is located in the heart of the sought-after village of Badwell Ash, an attractive Mid Suffolk village offering a range of local amenities, including a public house, fish and chip shop, village store and post office. The Village Hall has served as a multi-purpose community and recreation centre for more than 40 years. St Mary's Church, which has stood in Badwell Ash for almost 1,000 years, is believed to be the oldest building in the village. The earliest surviving section, the Chancel, is thought to date from the reign of Edward III in the early fourteenth century. The White Horse Inn, a charming 16th-century coaching inn, retains many original features and offers highly regarded gastro-pub dining in a welcoming atmosphere. The neighbouring villages of Norton and Walsham le Willows provide additional day-to-day amenities. Regular bus services operate from the village to nearby towns, while the A14 is less than a ten-minute drive away. More extensive shopping, leisure and educational facilities can be found in the historic cathedral town of Bury St Edmunds. Fern Avenue is perfectly positioned within the established residential setting of Jesmond, and situated close to the area's wide selection of shops, cafés, restaurants and leisure facilities, with Osborne Road providing a particularly well-known hub for dining and local amenities. Jesmond also benefits from access to Jesmond Dene and Jesmond Vale, providing extensive green space and walking routes nearby.
